#### Employing people during construction phase 

- Labour law is a head of power transferred to New Caledonia 

- – In 2010, a New Caledonian Labour Law Code was passed 

- – Identical to the pre-existing New Caledonian regulation 

- – Largely inspired by French law:  Protective of employees 

- – Special regime  dealing with Employment of Foreign Employees in the co

ntext of mining projects **construction** 

© 2013 Baker & McKenzie 

9 



##### <u>Special regime applying to foreign employees</u> assigned to New Caledonia by a foreign employer 

- Conditions of Employment (New Caledonian law)  Specific regime – NC law 2002 ( _Loi_ PSI) article LP 621-1 

- This regime is slightly more favorable for Employers 

   - Facilitation of overhours authorisation up to 60 hours per week (subject to conditions) 

   - Work permit facilitation 

– Only apply to foreign employees, assigned in New Caledonia by a foreign employer for the construction of mining or metallurgical projects or for works modifying the structure or infrastructure of mining or metallurgical activities. 

© 2013 Baker & McKenzie

#### Liability of the main contractor 

- French regulation imposes 10 years liability on certain construction work 

- Application of this 10 year building contractor liability in New Caledonia? Implicit application? 

- Main criteria: the type of the construction (building, industrial infrastructure, other) 

- Insurance issues 

- When contracting in an international context which law is applicable? 

© 2013 Baker & McKenzie 

12 



##### Obligation of the main contractor when subcontracting 

- Security of payment obligation of the main contractor toward the sub-contractor 

- Provide a Bank guarantee to secure payment 

- Mandatory statutory regulation (Law dated 31/01/1975 – applicable in NC since 1997!) 

- Failure to provide the bank guarantee may invalidate the subcontract agreement 

- Substantial risk if lump sum contract 

© 2013 Baker & McKenzie

#### Litigation – Arbitration - Mediation

#### Employing people during operation phase 

– We have seen that the special regime applies to employees, assigned in New Caledonia by a foreign employer for the <u>construction of mining or metallurgical projects or for works modifying the structure or infrastructure of mining or metallurgical</u> activities. 

- Consequence: at the end of the construction phase, the General regime applies: 

- Conditions of Employment  is the General regime applicable in New Caledonia: 

   - working hours: maximum of 10 hours d

aily, 40 hours weekly and 169 hours monthly; - Territorial or Industrial awards apply; - mandatory termination procedures. © 2013 Baker & McKenzie – 17 #### How is “construction phase” defined? - No legal or regulatory definition; - Discretion and flexibility of the Government in its determination of the construction phase; - Goro Project is a good example: - the end of the construction phase was set at June 2011 subject to exceptions; - First exception: for the Kwe Bassin, “construction” was extended until December 2011; - Second exception: companies involved in the ramp up benefited from an exemption until December 2011. © 2013 Baker & McKenzie 18 #### Employing people during operation phase – However the regulation indicates “works modifying the structure or infrastructure of mining or metallurgical activities” → fall under the Special Regime. – No definition of “works modifying the structure or infrastructure of mining or metallurgical activities” and no precedent. → Discretion of the Government. - It it likely that the following fall into the definition: - extension works;
